content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am trying to determine the exact switching and sensing voltage limits for [product_name] [version_no], but I am encountering conflicting specifications in various documents. Is there any resource that clearly states these restrictions? For example, can the 12/24V relay output of [product_name] switch 230V, and can each relay output be connected to a different live wire? Are the digital inputs able to handle 230V signals? Is it similar for [product_name] models with a 230V power supply? Thank you for any advice.

The relay outputs on [product_name] are normally open and potential-free, with eight terminals for four contacts. You can switch voltages from 0 to 230V AC/DC using these relays. The manual provides limits for voltage and current on the relays.
There is some ambiguity in the documentation regarding 'terminal groups.' It states that groups must be connected to the same phase, but does not clearly define which terminals belong to each group.

[user_name] mentioned that you can switch any voltage from 0 to 230V AC/DC with the relay outputs. Does that mean it is permitted to switch a 230VAC load using the isolated relay output of a 12/24V [product_name]? Are there any specific restrictions, such as a maximum of 48V for certain outputs?

You are asking plenty of questions about the [product_name] [article_no]. You can download manuals and online help for this version through the link: [url]. The relay technical data and other specifications are included in those documents.

There seems to be some misunderstanding. I only ask questions when the published documentation fails to provide answers, and I use these documents frequently. Any electrical engineer knows that a device should not be used for design purposes without clear isolation specifications. For example, the technical data for the 12/24 (or 24, 230) modules state 'Relay outputs, Electrical isolation Yes' and specify maximum switching current, but do not detail any parameters for 'isolated relay output.' So, how do I determine if it's legal to switch a 230VAC load using [product_name] 24 or 12/24 modules?

I'm sorry, but I am not clear on your question. The relays in the 12/24 version of [product_name] are electromechanical, not solid-state. This provides galvanic isolation between control voltage and switched contact. Each relay features a single normally open contact, they are potential-free and not interconnected. What is unclear about this?

For clarification: What is the validated isolation rating for the relay outputs on the following models: [product_name] 12/24RCE(o), 24CE(o), 24RCE(o), and 230RCE(o)? Is the isolation the same for all four relay output types? If so, where is this specification stated? Or can it differ by model, for example, 50V for some models and 500V for others? Appendix A.9 only notes a maximum switching current of 10A at 230VAC, but it does not specify limits for individual models.
If you have more questions like these, consider starting a support request. No forum user can provide guarantees about technical statements—best to ask [company_name] directly.

Hi, I think there has been a misunderstanding. Regarding relay outputs: All [product_name] Base and DM8/16 modules use the same types of relays. Every relay output is potential-free, allowing different voltages for each relay. Maximum load varies: Base modules handle 10A, DM8 or DM16 modules only 5A. From the manual (page 292): Insulation strength meets IEC61131-2 requirements. To know the test voltage, you will need the details from the IEC standard. For 230V inputs: Single-phase power—All 230V versions and DM8/16 230V modules require inputs to be connected to the same phase as the device supplies. Example: If powered by L1, the inputs must use L1. For three-phase power: The Base Module has two input groups. Inputs I1 to I4 must use the same phase as the power (e.g., L1), while I5 to I8 can use either the same phase or another one (L2 or L3). Supplying the device with L1 and connecting L2 to I1-I4 will cause damage, but L2 at I5-I8 will not. DM8/16 modules: Same rule applies. DM8 powered by L1—the four inputs must use L1 only. For three-phase setups: Base module powered by L1 means inputs I1-I4 use L1 and I5-I8 can use L2 or L3. A third phase can be used for DM8 power supply and inputs. Product details and illustrations can be found in the manuals. Hope this clarifies things.

[user_name], your summary of information from the manuals is excellent and helpful for users designing with [product_name]. Unfortunately, example connection diagrams are not official specifications and therefore unsuitable for legal design work. According to confirmation from [company_name] support, relay isolation information is not specified in the manuals. Work is ongoing.
Based on the support response, appendix A.9 'Switching capacity/service life of the relay outputs' defines this: Relay outputs can switch up to 240VAC, maximum 10A.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing challenges due to vague or inconsistent documentation regarding switching and sensing voltage limits, electrical isolation, and relay output ratings for various [product_name] modules. The absence of clearly defined technical data, particularly for isolation and legal usage, hinders user confidence in creating compliant electrical designs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are requesting clear, detailed documentation outlining electrical isolation, maximum switching and sensing voltages, and explicit legal usage guidelines for all [product_name] relay output models.
